subject: Post-call: Atlas Health eval playbook, dataset format & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Lin <rebecca@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Atlas Health eval playbook, dataset format & next steps

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — good alignment on goals. Below is a concise recap + concrete next steps so we can start your customer-specific eval on Redwood this week.

What we heard (high level)
- Primary objective: reliable clinical triage assistant that extracts structured findings and suggests next actions.
- Risk/constraints: dataset contains PHI, must follow Atlas security controls; latency target 300ms per token for interactive workloads; prefer solution under dedicated capacity.

Redwood recommended baseline models (based on initial prompts & latency targets)
- rwd/llama-3-70b-q4f (recommended for best instruction-following vs. hallucination tradeoff)
- rwd/opt-13b-8bit (cost-efficient baseline for throughput tests)
- open/gptj-6b-8bit (synthetic prompt stress testing)
Note: we will run the same eval harness across all candidates and surface token-cost + latency breakdowns.

Reference artifacts attached / links
- atlas_sample_prompts_v2.csv (attached) — small prompt set reflecting your triage flows
- atlas_sample_dataset_small.ndjson (attached) — sample dataset schema + 50 example items (anonymized)
- Redwood eval runbook (link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AtlasEvalPlaybook

Suggested dataset format & required fields
- NDJSON, UTF-8, one record per line
- Required fields: id, patient_id_hash, prompt, expected_response, task_type, annotations (list as JSON string), exposure_level (PHI | synthetic | public)
- Example: {"id": "a1", "patient_id_hash": "sha256:...", "prompt": "Summarize the note and recommend next step", "expected_response": "Urgent referral to pulmonology; order chest x-ray", "task_type": "extract_and_recommend", "annotations": "[{\"label\":\"finding\",\"span\":\"...\"}]", "exposure_level": "synthetic" }

Scoring rubric (proposed, can iterate)
- Primary metric: normalized exact-match on structured fields (match on canonicalized strings)
- Secondary metrics: token-level F1 for free-text recommendations, hallucination rate (asserted facts not in prompt), response latency (p50/p95), and per-response cost ($/k tokens)
- Thresholds to discuss: >= 92% structured-field match for go/no-go; hallucination < 3% for production rollout.

Security & PHI handling
- For PHI datasets we recommend either (1) an anonymized/synthetic subset for initial fit, or (2) run on Redwood Dedicated or Private with a customer-managed VPC.
- We'll share SOC2 and data-retention docs via the compliance link above.

Next steps (concrete dates)
1) You: share small anonymized sample (50–200 rows) by EOD 2026-02-18. (Samir / Rebecca)
2) We: provision project sandbox on Redwood and kick off baseline runs (rwd/opt-13b & rwd/llama-3-70b) by 2026-02-19. (Marissa)
3) Joint sync to review metrics & pick 1 model for deeper regression testing — propose 2026-02-20 10:00 PT (I'll send a calendar invite).

If that timeline works, I will attach a checklist and a short-run instruction set for your engineers to validate dataset formatting.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

Thanks Olga — this is very helpful and aligns with our expectations. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) PHI: we can provide an anonymized 100-row sample by 2026-02-18. For full runs we'll need to confirm the Dedicated/Private option and our legal team will loop in procurement.
2) Metrics: the 92% structured-field match threshold seems reasonable as an initial bar; can you confirm how strict the canonicalization step is (we have varied free-text templates across sites)?
3) SOC2: please attach the SOC2 PDF to the thread if possible; we need it for our security questionnaire.

We'll aim to make the sample available on the share link you provided. Also looping Samir since he'll own the dataset handoff.

Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800

Rebecca — quick answers and attachments: 

- Canonicalization: our scorer uses a two-stage normalization pipeline (lowercase + medical abbreviation expansion + whitespace/token normalization). For structured fields we also support mapping tables if you share canonical labels (e.g., ICD-10 / internal codes). If you'd like, Marissa can help map your templates to the canonical table during the first run.
- SOC2: uploaded to drive and link included here: https://redwood-internal.example.com/compliance/soc2-report.pdf (also attached for convenience).
- PHI handling: if you prefer, we can run the baseline on a syntheticized variant we generate from your sample and report back results before moving to Dedicated. That reduces initial overhead for procurement.

I've attached: atlas_sample_prompts_v2.csv, atlas_sample_dataset_small.ndjson, redwood_eval_schema.md (small runbook). Marissa — can you provision the project workspace (project id: atlas-eval-ATLAS-472) and kick off baseline runs once Samir confirms upload?

Olga
